newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks finish flat despite tumbling golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks finish flat despite tumbling golds.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index ended a quiet Friday almost flat as slim gains in most of its sectors balanced a 3.3 percent drop in the influential gold group.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index only shed 2.60 points to close at 6585.44 points. Trading was light at 70 million shares worth C$1.2 billion ($640 million) as U.S. markets remained shut for Independence Day festivities.
"The real reason is the gold price," said Maison Placements Canada president John Ing. "That's the real thing that hurt the market."
Toronto's heavily weighted golds extended yesterday's fall as the gold bullion price dropped $8.10 to $325.45 in London, almost touching a 12-year low.
The Reserve Bank of Australia said on Thursday it sold 167 tonnes of gold to reduce holdings, raising fears that other central banks may follow suit.
However eight of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes continued to gain ground after Thursday's rally, led by utilities, transportation and retail.
Besides golds, conglomerates and media slipped.
Declining issues edged out advances 462 to 454 while 283 finished flat.
"The market volumes were constrained by the absence of New York," Ing said. "Most people were talking about activities other than the stock market."
Brokerage Wood Gundy held a golf tournament, and a trader noted that "obviously it was pretty quiet."
Over the week Canada's largest equities market added a sizeable 153 points, or about 2.4 percent, from Monday's open of 6432.55.
* The major gold companies which suffered the most were Placer Dome Inc., whose shares dropped 1.25 to 20.45, and Barrick Gold Corp. which fell 1.10 to 28.20.

* Shares in Grandma Lee's Inc. continued their winning ways from Monday, adding six and a half cents to reach 0.275. At the beginning of the week the restaurant chain operator announced it would modify its strategy to expand its outlets and bring aboard new concepts, to soon post its first real profitable quarter.
